content.comment_body: My [product_name] module is connected to a [product_name] base module. I've attempted several times to send commands for switching network inputs based on their VMs, but each time I receive a 'No success' response. Could this be due to outdated firmware? My current firmware is [version_no].
The BIT (Bool) data format for SMS instructions is supported only starting from firmware [version_no]. You can download the latest firmware ([version_no]) for free. [document]
Please share the exact command you used in your SMS.

The connection between the devices appears to be working, as the STATUS=RUN/STOP command functions correctly. I've tried various commands, such as: [Password=A] Command: A;[product_name]=VM1,1,BYTE Reply: [product_name]=VM1,1,BYTE: No Success Command: A;[product_name]=VM1,1,BIT Reply: [product_name]=VM1,1,BIT: Invalid Parameter Command: A;[product_name]=VM1,1,WORD Reply: [product_name]=VM1,1,WORD: No Success [diagram attached]

To use the BIT datatype correctly, try the following syntax: - Password;[product_name]=VM6.0,1,BIT for setting the 1-signal - Password;[product_name]=VM6.0,0,BIT for setting the 0-signal This will set the VM-Bit V6.0 high or low. Similarly: - Password;[product_name]=VM6.7,1,BIT for 1-signal - Password;[product_name]=VM6.7,0,BIT for 0-signal This controls VM-Bit V6.7 high or low. The BIT datatype is only supported from firmware [version_no] and above. Is your device configured in the WBM for receiving SMS? Are both devices on the same IP address segment?

As previously mentioned, the connection works fine—I can send STATUS=RUN/STOP commands. My firmware is [version_no]. How can I issue commands using the BYTE data type? See the attached diagram for reference.
The correct syntax for using the BYTE datatype is: - Password;[product_name]=VM6,1,BYTE to set 1-signal - Password;[product_name]=VM6,0,BYTE to set 0-signal This will switch VM-Bit V6.0 high or low.
It's still not working! Command: Password;[product_name]=VM6,1,BYTE Reply: [product_name]=VM6,1,BYTE: No Success [diagram attached]
You have the correct syntax. Unfortunately, I'm unable to assist further—perhaps another community member can help.
Is anyone else able to assist?
Are you sure you're following the instructions provided by [user_name]? There may be an issue in how you're entering the codes. Thanks,
Just checking—did you replace 'Password' with your actual password when sending the command? If so, perhaps try updating the firmware, since no other known solutions have worked yet.
He mentioned he can set the device to RUN or STOP mode via SMS and knows to replace PASSWORD with the actual password. If it were me, I'd start a support request.
I encountered a similar issue—the phone added a blank space after the command, resulting in 'invalid command/syntax' errors. It took a while before I found the cause.

Hello everyone, I faced a similar issue a few months ago and received the 'Not successful' message. After trying various solutions with no luck, I performed a factory reset on both devices and that resolved the problem! I'm not sure why, but it worked.
I've updated the firmware to the latest version ([version_no]), but the problem still persists. Factory resetting both devices also hasn't helped.

It may be time to initiate a support request. There's an example on the [company_name] website that shows how to use [product_name] with [product_name]. You might want to simulate that example to see if it works. I hope you find a solution.

Hi, have you tried the factory reset as suggested by [user_name]? If so, what was the result? Additionally, could you try the example from the application resources mentioned by [user_name]? Please update us with the outcome.

Have you programmed the outputs in the [product_name] module via its webpage? STATUS=RUN/STOP is standard, but for writing outputs, you need to configure this on the device's webpage. Follow the steps in this resource: [url]
Hello, You’ll receive 'No success' if the change isn’t defined for the [product_name]. It must be set up and accessible from the module; then it can be changed via SMS. [user_name]
Thank you so much! I finally found the solution in the PDF file.
Earlier, I asked if you have set up everything in the WBM and attached an overview of what needs to be done.
You're right, I missed that suggestion. I thought all the configuration in WBM was just entering the IP for the [product_name] base module.
Have you solved the issue, or do you still need a solution?

analysis.insight_summary: Users continually encounter problems sending SMS commands to control network inputs on [product_name] hardware via the [product_name] communication module. Although the SMS syntax is correct and the connection works for other commands, instructions using BIT and BYTE formats fail, often returning errors like 'No Success.' Investigation reveals a firmware limitation—the required data types are supported only in firmware [version_no] or newer, causing confusion and operational difficulties without clear UI guidance regarding compatibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to control network inputs on the device via SMS commands using different data types (BIT, BYTE, WORD) and correct syntax, regardless of firmware version. They also anticipate receiving clear feedback about any unsupported data types or outdated firmware, enabling quick troubleshooting and resolution.
feature_keywords: BIT and BYTE data type support
